title: Technology Sector Update for 07/13/2018: ACIA,OCLR,AAPL,GOGO,PIXY - Nasdaq.com
text:

Technology stocks closed narrowly lower Friday afternoon, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 losing less than 0.1% in value while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a 0.4% decline.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Acacia Communications ( ACIA ) was hanging on to a nearly 1% gain late in Friday trading, returning most of a 3% spike for the networking equipment company that followed the U.S. Department of Commerce this afternoon lifting its ban on U.S. companies selling to Chinese hardware and smartphone manufacturer ZTE. ZTE is expected to begin rebuilding its business after paying the final $400 million tranche of its $1.4 billion penalty to resolve charges it sold U.S. technology into Iran and North Korea in violation of U.S.-led sanctions. The end of the ZTE ban also had a positve impact on Oclaro ( OCLR ), another ZTE supplier, whose stock climbed almost 1% after the government's announcement although it since has slipped back below its Thursday closing price of $9.07 a share.
In other sector news:
+ ShiftPixy ( PIXY ) soared over 90% higher on Friday after the staffing software firm issued preliminary fiscal Q3 financial results, projecting a net loss of $0.06 per share for the three months ended May 31, improving a $0.11 per share net loss during the year-earlier period, as revenue more than doubled year-over-year, rising to $9.4 million from $4.6 million last year. The workforce platform company also said gross billings more than doubled over last year to $60.2 million, compared to $27.5 million for the March-to-May reporting period in 2017.
+ Apple ( AAPL ) was slightly higher Friday, topping out with a 0.4% rise, after the technology giant disclosed plans to launch a clean energy fund in China that will connect suppliers with renewable energy sources as part of efforts to address climate change. The company said the $300 million China Clean Energy Fund will invest in and develop renewable energy and alternative fuels projects totaling more than 1 gigawatt of renewable energy in China, the equivalent of powering nearly 1 million homes. The fund also looks to provide participants with the advantage of greater purchasing power and realizing more attractive and diverse clean energy solutions.
- Gogo ( GOGO ) retreated Friday, sinking as much as 18%, despite the in-flight connectivity company reiterating its FY18 revenue guidance, saying it is set to reach free cash flow break-even by 2020 as well as generating significant yearly EBITDA growth seen rising to more than $200 million in 2022. CEO Oakleigh Thorne said the recent initiatives are positioning Gogo for sustainable value creation, adding he expects to reduce cash burn at the company by over $100 million in FY19 from prior-year levels and by a further $100 million in 2020. The firm maintained its revenue target of $865 million to $935 million for 2018, in line with its prior guidance and market expectations for $885.96 million in revenue this year.
